# M01 — I01 Lock Scientific Authority and Core Production Configuration

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M01 — Scientific Configuration & Repository Contract
- **Primary deliverable:** Lock Scientific Authority and Core Production Configuration
- **Issue type:** Infrastructure / Implementation
- **Milestone outcome served:** A validated production configuration and canonical repository/test structure encode every roadmap-fixed scientific value, ownership boundary, and implementation-readiness invariant.
- **Atomic requirement count:** 153

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- Authority; §3 support lock
- Configuration YAML and fixed scientific configuration blocks

### Requirements

- REQ-0004, REQ-0007, REQ-0105–REQ-0106, REQ-0253–REQ-0341, REQ-0491–REQ-0514, REQ-0524–REQ-0527, REQ-0554–REQ-0571, REQ-0651–REQ-0654, REQ-2814–REQ-2815, REQ-2818–REQ-2822, REQ-2835–REQ-2837
## Objective

Deliver **Lock Scientific Authority and Core Production Configuration** as a complete, reviewable, testable unit of M01. The completed implementation must realize the roadmap-defined behavior for every mapped atomic requirement, preserve the approved milestone boundary, and produce the validation and evidence needed by downstream issues without requiring those issues to reinterpret or rediscover this scope.

## Scope

Implement only the work required to satisfy the referenced roadmap requirements:

- **Scientific authority and no-post-hoc configuration lock** — roadmap scope `Authority; §3 support lock`; requirements `REQ-0004, REQ-0007, REQ-0105–REQ-0106`.
- **Core scientific, data, detector, context, projection and evidence configuration** — roadmap scope `Configuration YAML and fixed scientific configuration blocks`; requirements `REQ-0253–REQ-0341, REQ-0491–REQ-0514, REQ-0524–REQ-0527, REQ-0554–REQ-0571, REQ-0651–REQ-0654, REQ-2814–REQ-2815, REQ-2818–REQ-2822, REQ-2835–REQ-2837`.

The mapped requirement types are: Configuration (132), Failure Semantics (8), Training (6), Statistical Analysis (3), Preprocessing (2), Mathematics (1), Reproducibility (1).

No requirement may exist only implicitly in tests, acceptance criteria, or implementation notes; the atomic acceptance checklist below is part of the executable scope.

## Implementation Requirements

- Implement and verify **Scientific authority and no-post-hoc configuration lock** exactly as specified by `Authority; §3 support lock`. Required evidence contract: Typed-config tests reject external overrides, undocumented defaults, and post-hoc scientific choices.
- Implement and verify **Core scientific, data, detector, context, projection and evidence configuration** exactly as specified by `Configuration YAML and fixed scientific configuration blocks`. Required evidence contract: Load the production configuration through the typed schema; assert every exact value/grid and canonical digest.

All implementation details below are mandatory where defined by the mapped atomic requirements. The implementation must expose typed, deterministic, testable contracts rather than relying on undocumented convention.
## Implementation Surface

Expected areas affected by this issue:

### Production Code

- Roadmap-defined production modules that own Configuration, Failure Semantics, Training, Statistical Analysis, Preprocessing behavior for the listed requirements.
- Canonical domain/application implementations required by the mapped work packages; exact paths and ownership rules are those explicitly enumerated by the atomic requirements.

### Configuration / Domain Contracts

- Typed configuration, enums, frozen domain models, validation rules, scientific constants, and protocol identities required by the mapped atomic requirements.
- Configuration/protocol digests and cross-field validation wherever the roadmap declares them material.

### CLI / Application Surface

- Only CLI/application behavior explicitly required by the mapped requirements or necessary to invoke the owning application service.
- No scientific algorithm, statistical procedure, dataset construction logic, or artifact-layout logic is implemented in CLI commands.

### Tests

- Unit, scientific, architecture, integration, end-to-end, smoke, determinism, provenance, failure-path, and regression tests applicable to the mapped requirements.
- Golden or numerical fixtures where exact formulas, canonicalization, hashes, seeds, thresholds, or deterministic identities are specified.

### Artifacts / Reporting

- All persisted artifacts, manifests, checkpoints, caches, results, source-data files, tables, figures, claim records, status evidence, and reproducibility exports explicitly required by the mapped atomic requirements.
- No manually copied scientific result values.

## Objective

Deliver **Establish Canonical Repository, Source and Test Structure** as a complete, reviewable, testable unit of M01. The completed implementation must realize the roadmap-defined behavior for every mapped atomic requirement, preserve the approved milestone boundary, and produce the validation and evidence needed by downstream issues without requiring those issues to reinterpret or rediscover this scope.

## Scope

Implement only the work required to satisfy the referenced roadmap requirements:

- **Canonical repository, output, results and documentation tree** — roadmap scope `§16 repository structure`; requirements `REQ-1556–REQ-1671`.
- **Source-package and public CLI module tree** — roadmap scope `§16 repository structure`; requirements `REQ-1672–REQ-1803`.
- **Architecture, unit, scientific, integration, end-to-end and smoke test tree** — roadmap scope `§16 repository structure`; requirements `REQ-1804–REQ-1877`.

The mapped requirement types are: Architecture (243), Testing (76), Configuration (3).

No requirement may exist only implicitly in tests, acceptance criteria, or implementation notes; the atomic acceptance checklist below is part of the executable scope.
## Dependencies

### Blocked By

- I01 — Lock Scientific Authority and Core Production Configuration: provides the locked configuration, repository architecture, and readiness contract required by this work.

### Blocks

- I06 — Enforce Architecture Invariants and Implementation Readiness: consumes the validated contracts, artifacts, or evidence produced by this issue.
## Implementation Requirements

- Implement and verify **Canonical repository, output, results and documentation tree** exactly as specified by `§16 repository structure`. Required evidence contract: Structural inventory tests verify every required path and role.
- Implement and verify **Source-package and public CLI module tree** exactly as specified by `§16 repository structure`. Required evidence contract: Package/import/architecture tests verify all required modules and public ownership boundaries.
- Implement and verify **Architecture, unit, scientific, integration, end-to-end and smoke test tree** exactly as specified by `§16 repository structure`. Required evidence contract: Test-structure checks verify every required test path is present and discoverable.

All implementation details below are mandatory where defined by the mapped atomic requirements. The implementation must expose typed, deterministic, testable contracts rather than relying on undocumented convention.
## Implementation Surface

Expected areas affected by this issue:

### Production Code

- Roadmap-defined production modules that own Architecture, Testing, Configuration behavior for the listed requirements.
- Canonical domain/application implementations required by the mapped work packages; exact paths and ownership rules are those explicitly enumerated by the atomic requirements.

### Configuration / Domain Contracts

- Typed configuration, enums, frozen domain models, validation rules, scientific constants, and protocol identities required by the mapped atomic requirements.
- Configuration/protocol digests and cross-field validation wherever the roadmap declares them material.

### CLI / Application Surface

- Only CLI/application behavior explicitly required by the mapped requirements or necessary to invoke the owning application service.
- No scientific algorithm, statistical procedure, dataset construction logic, or artifact-layout logic is implemented in CLI commands.

### Tests

- Unit, scientific, architecture, integration, end-to-end, smoke, determinism, provenance, failure-path, and regression tests applicable to the mapped requirements.
- Golden or numerical fixtures where exact formulas, canonicalization, hashes, seeds, thresholds, or deterministic identities are specified.

### Artifacts / Reporting

- All persisted artifacts, manifests, checkpoints, caches, results, source-data files, tables, figures, claim records, status evidence, and reproducibility exports explicitly required by the mapped atomic requirements.
- No manually copied scientific result values.

### Roadmap-Direct Architecture Acceptance Criteria

The §16 repository tree states that these test responsibilities are part of the implementation architecture even where the Coverage Inventory atomized only the test path. They are therefore binding roadmap-direct obligations in this issue.

- [ ] `test_dependency_boundaries.py` enforces allowed dependency directions between architectural layers and prevents architectural responsibility violations.
- [ ] `test_public_type_boundaries.py` ensures public, domain, and application APIs use explicit meaningful types rather than loosely typed interfaces or inappropriate raw primitives.
- [ ] `test_no_any_dict_object.py` rejects inappropriate use of `Any`, `object`, and anonymous dict-based domain/configuration/artifact payloads except narrowly justified external-library boundaries.
- [ ] `test_no_primitive_leaks.py` detects inappropriate `str`/`int`/`float`/`bool`/`list`/`dict` primitives crossing domain or architectural boundaries, including primitive public inputs and outputs where meaningful domain types should be used.
- [ ] `test_no_hardcoded_values.py` detects hardcoded scientific, experimental, statistical, dataset, seed, threshold, algorithm, protocol, and other governed values outside their authoritative owner.
- [ ] `test_configuration_ownership.py` ensures configuration values have one authoritative owner and are not repeated or copied into constants, implementation code, CLI defaults, tests, or parallel configuration structures.
- [ ] `test_no_duplicate_constants.py` detects duplicate constants and equivalent independently maintained values across the repository.
- [ ] `test_dead_code.py` detects dead, unused, unreachable, obsolete, and superseded production modules, classes, functions, methods, constants, and other symbols.
- [ ] `test_enum_integrity.py` detects unused enums and ensures authoritative enums are actually used rather than bypassed by equivalent free-form strings or duplicate identities.
- [ ] `test_naming_policy.py` enforces descriptive names for modules, classes, functions, methods, variables, and parameters and rejects vague, generic, strange, misleading, or unjustifiably short names and abbreviations.
- [ ] `test_canonical_vocabulary.py` enforces canonical project, scientific, algorithm, dataset, policy, experiment, artifact, and architectural terminology and rejects stale aliases, obsolete terminology, opaque names, and artificial version naming.
- [ ] `test_no_comments_or_docstrings.py` rejects Python source comments and module/class/function/method docstrings.
- [ ] `test_no_todos_or_temporary_code.py` rejects TODO, FIXME, HACK, XXX, commented-out implementations, temporary markers, unfinished code residue, and similar development leftovers.
- [ ] `test_static_typing.py` runs repository-wide strict Pyright across production and tests so Pyright/Pylance-visible typing violations fail the test suite.
- [ ] `test_dependency_hygiene.py` enforces dependency hygiene and detects unused, missing, or incorrectly declared dependencies.

# M02 — I10 Implement Semantic Identity, Dependency Graph and Material Fingerprints

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M02 — Artifact Runtime, Provenance & Execution Orchestration
- **Primary deliverable:** Implement Semantic Identity, Dependency Graph and Material Fingerprints
- **Issue type:** Infrastructure / Implementation
- **Milestone outcome served:** The project can deterministically identify, validate, reuse, invalidate, resume, recover, and orchestrate scientific artifacts and experiment cells under the roadmap's artifact-first provenance contract.
- **Atomic requirement count:** 67

## Roadmap Authority

- §17.1–§17.3

### Requirements

- REQ-2044, REQ-2045, REQ-2046, REQ-2047, REQ-2048, REQ-2049, REQ-2050, REQ-2051, REQ-2052, REQ-2053, REQ-2054, REQ-2055, REQ-2056
## Objective

Deliver **Implement Semantic Identity, Dependency Graph and Material Fingerprints** as a complete, reviewable, testable unit of M02. The completed implementation must realize the roadmap-defined behavior for every mapped atomic requirement, preserve the approved milestone boundary, and produce the validation and evidence needed by downstream issues without requiring those issues to reinterpret or rediscover this scope.

## Scope

Implement only the work required to satisfy the referenced roadmap requirements:

- **Semantic identity, dependency graph and material fingerprints** — roadmap scope `§17.1–§17.3`; requirements `REQ-1990–REQ-2056`.

The mapped requirement types are: Provenance (54), Failure Semantics (13).

No requirement may exist only implicitly in tests, acceptance criteria, or implementation notes; the atomic acceptance checklist below is part of the executable scope.
## Dependencies

### Blocked By

- I07 — Implement Artifact-First Execution Lifecycle: provides validated artifact identity, provenance, lifecycle, reuse/invalidation, and orchestration contracts consumed here.
- I08 — Implement Canonical Serialization, Hashing and Seed Derivation: provides validated artifact identity, provenance, lifecycle, reuse/invalidation, and orchestration contracts consumed here.

## Implementation Requirements

- Implement and verify **Semantic identity, dependency graph and material fingerprints** exactly as specified by `§17.1–§17.3`. Required evidence contract: Identity/fingerprint tests prove semantic filenames and material dependency hashes change only when material inputs change.

All implementation details below are mandatory where defined by the mapped atomic requirements. The implementation must expose typed, deterministic, testable contracts rather than relying on undocumented convention.
## Implementation Surface

Expected areas affected by this issue:

### Production Code

- Roadmap-defined production modules that own Provenance, Failure Semantics behavior for the listed requirements.
- Canonical domain/application implementations required by the mapped work packages; exact paths and ownership rules are those explicitly enumerated by the atomic requirements.

### Configuration / Domain Contracts

- Typed configuration, enums, frozen domain models, validation rules, scientific constants, and protocol identities required by the mapped atomic requirements.
- Configuration/protocol digests and cross-field validation wherever the roadmap declares them material.

### CLI / Application Surface

- Only CLI/application behavior explicitly required by the mapped requirements or necessary to invoke the owning application service.
- No scientific algorithm, statistical procedure, dataset construction logic, or artifact-layout logic is implemented in CLI commands.

### Tests

- Unit, scientific, architecture, integration, end-to-end, smoke, determinism, provenance, failure-path, and regression tests applicable to the mapped requirements.
- Golden or numerical fixtures where exact formulas, canonicalization, hashes, seeds, thresholds, or deterministic identities are specified.

### Artifacts / Reporting

- All persisted artifacts, manifests, checkpoints, caches, results, source-data files, tables, figures, claim records, status evidence, and reproducibility exports explicitly required by the mapped atomic requirements.
- No manually copied scientific result values.

## Objective

Deliver **Implement Compatibility, Selective Invalidation, Recovery and Execution States** as a complete, reviewable, testable unit of M02. The completed implementation must realize the roadmap-defined behavior for every mapped atomic requirement, preserve the approved milestone boundary, and produce the validation and evidence needed by downstream issues without requiring those issues to reinterpret or rediscover this scope.

## Scope

Implement only the work required to satisfy the referenced roadmap requirements:

- **Compatibility, selective invalidation and execution states** — roadmap scope `§17.4–§17.6`; requirements `REQ-2057–REQ-2102, REQ-2970–REQ-2973`.
- **Recovery, checkpoints, caches, logging and dependency index** — roadmap scope `§17.7–§17.9`; requirements `REQ-2103–REQ-2147`.

The mapped requirement types are: Failure Semantics (73), Provenance (19), Reproducibility (3).

No requirement may exist only implicitly in tests, acceptance criteria, or implementation notes; the atomic acceptance checklist below is part of the executable scope.

## Implementation Surface

Expected areas affected by this issue:

### Production Code

- Roadmap-defined production modules that own Failure Semantics, Provenance, Reproducibility behavior for the listed requirements.
- Canonical domain/application implementations required by the mapped work packages; exact paths and ownership rules are those explicitly enumerated by the atomic requirements.

- Typed configuration, enums, frozen domain models, validation rules, scientific constants, and protocol identities required by the mapped atomic requirements.

### CLI / Application Surface

- Only CLI/application behavior explicitly required by the mapped requirements or necessary to invoke the owning application service.
- No scientific algorithm, statistical procedure, dataset construction logic, or artifact-layout logic is implemented in CLI commands.

- Unit, scientific, architecture, integration, end-to-end, smoke, determinism, provenance, failure-path, and regression tests applicable to the mapped requirements.

### Artifacts / Reporting

- All persisted artifacts, manifests, checkpoints, caches, results, source-data files, tables, figures, claim records, status evidence, and reproducibility exports explicitly required by the mapped atomic requirements.
- No manually copied scientific result values.

## Required Tests

### Issue-Specific Verification

- [ ] Work-package verification for **Compatibility, selective invalidation and execution states**: Fault-injection tests verify provenance compatibility, atomic completion, selective invalidation, and exact state namespaces.
- [ ] Work-package verification for **Recovery, checkpoints, caches, logging and dependency index**: Recovery tests verify retries, repair, descendant cleanup, compatible checkpoints/caches, structured logs, and dependency-index integrity.
## Required Outputs

- [ ] Verified implementation and evidence package for **Compatibility, selective invalidation and execution states**, including every roadmap-mandated artifact, schema, manifest, result, CLI behavior, table/figure, or validation output enumerated by the mapped atomic requirements.
- [ ] Verified implementation and evidence package for **Recovery, checkpoints, caches, logging and dependency index**, including every roadmap-mandated artifact, schema, manifest, result, CLI behavior, table/figure, or validation output enumerated by the mapped atomic requirements.

All implementation details below are mandatory where defined by the mapped atomic requirements. The implementation must expose typed, deterministic, testable contracts rather than relying on undocumented convention.
## Implementation Surface

Expected areas affected by this issue:

### Production Code

- Roadmap-defined production modules that own Provenance, Artifact, Reproducibility, Reporting, Statistical Analysis behavior for the listed requirements.
- Canonical domain/application implementations required by the mapped work packages; exact paths and ownership rules are those explicitly enumerated by the atomic requirements.

### Configuration / Domain Contracts

- Typed configuration, enums, frozen domain models, validation rules, scientific constants, and protocol identities required by the mapped atomic requirements.
- Configuration/protocol digests and cross-field validation wherever the roadmap declares them material.

### CLI / Application Surface

- Only CLI/application behavior explicitly required by the mapped requirements or necessary to invoke the owning application service.
- No scientific algorithm, statistical procedure, dataset construction logic, or artifact-layout logic is implemented in CLI commands.

### Tests

- Unit, scientific, architecture, integration, end-to-end, smoke, determinism, provenance, failure-path, and regression tests applicable to the mapped requirements.
- Golden or numerical fixtures where exact formulas, canonicalization, hashes, seeds, thresholds, or deterministic identities are specified.

### Artifacts / Reporting

- All persisted artifacts, manifests, checkpoints, caches, results, source-data files, tables, figures, claim records, status evidence, and reproducibility exports explicitly required by the mapped atomic requirements.
- No manually copied scientific result values.

# M03 — I13 Implement ODI, EMII and Fixed Scientific Definitions

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M03 — Scientific Definitions, Generators & Reference Methods
- **Primary deliverable:** Implement ODI, EMII and Fixed Scientific Definitions
- **Issue type:** Implementation / Validation
- **Milestone outcome served:** The ODI/EMII theory, deterministic synthetic generators, controlled campaign families, and fixed comparator/reference methods are implemented as numerically verifiable scientific primitives.
- **Atomic requirement count:** 18

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §2.1–§2.2
- Scientific definitions/derivations

### Requirements

- REQ-0052, REQ-0053, REQ-0054, REQ-0055, REQ-0056, REQ-0057, REQ-0058, REQ-0059, REQ-0060, REQ-0061, REQ-0062, REQ-0063, REQ-0064, REQ-0065, REQ-0487, REQ-0488, REQ-0489, REQ-0490
## Objective

Deliver **Implement ODI, EMII and Fixed Scientific Definitions** as a complete, reviewable, testable unit of M03. The completed implementation must realize the roadmap-defined behavior for every mapped atomic requirement, preserve the approved milestone boundary, and produce the validation and evidence needed by downstream issues without requiring those issues to reinterpret or rediscover this scope.

## Scope

Implement only the work required to satisfy the referenced roadmap requirements:

- **ODI and EMII formal definitions** — roadmap scope `§2.1–§2.2`; requirements `REQ-0052–REQ-0065`.
- **Fixed scientific method rules** — roadmap scope `Scientific definitions/derivations`; requirements `REQ-0487–REQ-0490`.

The mapped requirement types are: Mathematics (12), Algorithm (3), Claim Boundary (2), Configuration (1).

No requirement may exist only implicitly in tests, acceptance criteria, or implementation notes; the atomic acceptance checklist below is part of the executable scope.
## Dependencies

### Blocked By

- I06 — Enforce Architecture Invariants and Implementation Readiness: provides the locked configuration, repository architecture, and readiness contract required by this work.
- I12 — Implement Evidence Lifecycle, Provenance Schemas and Confirmatory Execution Roles: provides validated artifact identity, provenance, lifecycle, reuse/invalidation, and orchestration contracts consumed here.

### Blocks

- I14 — Implement Deterministic Synthetic Generators and Campaign Families: consumes the validated contracts, artifacts, or evidence produced by this issue.
- I15 — Implement Exclusion-Matched Dependence and HOFD Reference Methods: consumes the validated contracts, artifacts, or evidence produced by this issue.
- I16 — Implement Strong Comparator and Sequential Reference Methods: consumes the validated contracts, artifacts, or evidence produced by this issue.
- I27 — Implement Exclusion-Matched Information Fields, Ranks and Context Conditioning: consumes the validated contracts, artifacts, or evidence produced by this issue.
## Implementation Requirements

- Implement and verify **ODI and EMII formal definitions** exactly as specified by `§2.1–§2.2`. Required evidence contract: Hand-computed/property tests verify exact formulas, strict inequalities, admissible-information rules, and stopping semantics.
- Implement and verify **Fixed scientific method rules** exactly as specified by `Scientific definitions/derivations`. Required evidence contract: Deterministic unit/numerical tests exercise each fixed derivation and prohibited alternative choice.

All implementation details below are mandatory where defined by the mapped atomic requirements. The implementation must expose typed, deterministic, testable contracts rather than relying on undocumented convention.
## Implementation Surface

Expected areas affected by this issue:

### Production Code

- Roadmap-defined production modules that own Mathematics, Algorithm, Claim Boundary, Configuration behavior for the listed requirements.
- Canonical domain/application implementations required by the mapped work packages; exact paths and ownership rules are those explicitly enumerated by the atomic requirements.

### Configuration / Domain Contracts

- Typed configuration, enums, frozen domain models, validation rules, scientific constants, and protocol identities required by the mapped atomic requirements.
- Configuration/protocol digests and cross-field validation wherever the roadmap declares them material.

### CLI / Application Surface

- Only CLI/application behavior explicitly required by the mapped requirements or necessary to invoke the owning application service.
- No scientific algorithm, statistical procedure, dataset construction logic, or artifact-layout logic is implemented in CLI commands.

### Tests

- Unit, scientific, architecture, integration, end-to-end, smoke, determinism, provenance, failure-path, and regression tests applicable to the mapped requirements.
- Golden or numerical fixtures where exact formulas, canonicalization, hashes, seeds, thresholds, or deterministic identities are specified.

### Artifacts / Reporting

- All persisted artifacts, manifests, checkpoints, caches, results, source-data files, tables, figures, claim records, status evidence, and reproducibility exports explicitly required by the mapped atomic requirements.
- No manually copied scientific result values.

## Objective

Deliver **Materialize Dataset, Protocol, Detector, Baseline and Experiment Result Tables** as a complete, reviewable, testable unit of M10. The completed implementation must realize the roadmap-defined behavior for every mapped atomic requirement, preserve the approved milestone boundary, and produce the validation and evidence needed by downstream issues without requiring those issues to reinterpret or rediscover this scope.

## Scope

Implement only the work required to satisfy the referenced roadmap requirements:

- **Source-data, dataset-role, protocol, detector and baseline tables** — roadmap scope `§20.1–§20.5`; requirements `REQ-2421–REQ-2488`.
- **Experiment result tables and machine-readable source data** — roadmap scope `§20.6–§20.10`; requirements `REQ-2489–REQ-2654`.

The mapped requirement types are: Reporting (234).

No requirement may exist only implicitly in tests, acceptance criteria, or implementation notes; the atomic acceptance checklist below is part of the executable scope.

## Implementation Requirements

- Implement and verify **Source-data, dataset-role, protocol, detector and baseline tables** exactly as specified by `§20.1–§20.5`. Required evidence contract: Table-contract tests assert exact source paths/columns/roles/precision and trace every value to current machine-readable artifacts.
- Implement and verify **Experiment result tables and machine-readable source data** exactly as specified by `§20.6–§20.10`. Required evidence contract: Per-experiment table/source-data validators cover every required result family and reject stale/incomplete inputs.

All implementation details below are mandatory where defined by the mapped atomic requirements. The implementation must expose typed, deterministic, testable contracts rather than relying on undocumented convention.
## Implementation Surface

Expected areas affected by this issue:

### Production Code

- Roadmap-defined production modules that own Reporting behavior for the listed requirements.
- Canonical domain/application implementations required by the mapped work packages; exact paths and ownership rules are those explicitly enumerated by the atomic requirements.

### Configuration / Domain Contracts

- Typed configuration, enums, frozen domain models, validation rules, scientific constants, and protocol identities required by the mapped atomic requirements.
- Configuration/protocol digests and cross-field validation wherever the roadmap declares them material.

### CLI / Application Surface

- Only CLI/application behavior explicitly required by the mapped requirements or necessary to invoke the owning application service.
- No scientific algorithm, statistical procedure, dataset construction logic, or artifact-layout logic is implemented in CLI commands.

### Tests

- Unit, scientific, architecture, integration, end-to-end, smoke, determinism, provenance, failure-path, and regression tests applicable to the mapped requirements.
- Golden or numerical fixtures where exact formulas, canonicalization, hashes, seeds, thresholds, or deterministic identities are specified.

### Artifacts / Reporting

- All persisted artifacts, manifests, checkpoints, caches, results, source-data files, tables, figures, claim records, status evidence, and reproducibility exports explicitly required by the mapped atomic requirements.
- No manually copied scientific result values.
